name: Bimetric-Screened-Frame: Independent Stiff-Vector with e^-y PPN Decoupling from F+ Nonlocality
claimed_mechanism: Uses a Hassan-Rosen bimetric chassis to provide a massive graviton sector that can source off-ray lensing without a preferred frame, while a separate screened stiff vector u_mu provides the local e^-y suppressed PPN preferred-frame effects. The vector's kinetic term is independent of the e^-y screening factor, avoiding the P7 strong-coupling wall that killed khronometric MOND. The spatial F+ kernel handles the global MOND force law without localizing the frame-breaking term.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the bimetric slip provides the necessary lensing enhancement (eta~1) without the f(R) delta-R ray lock of DC-013. The screened vector contributes alpha_1, alpha_2 ~ e^-y, which are exponentially small in the Solar System (y~10^5) but unsuppressed in the galactic MOND regime (y~1). The nonlocal F+ kernel ensures the MOND force law ∇·[μ∇Φ]=4πGρ is satisfied globally.
inequivalence_argument: Distinct from DC-001 (has preferred_frame=true coupling with e^-y screening AND spatial nonlocality, plus a second metric). Distinct from DC-002 (uses a bimetric chassis, not a 6-DOF aether; the vector is stiff and screened, not a constant K_B aether). Distinct from DC-010 (the vector's kinetic normalization is independent of the e^-y screening factor, so alpha->0 does not send the kinetic term to zero, avoiding the P7/strong-coupling wall that killed finite-alpha_inf khronometric). Distinct from DC-012/DC-013 (has a preferred-frame carrier, so not frame-free; the bimetric slip evades the delta-R ray lock). Distinct from DC-011 (does not localize the F+ kernel; uses a genuine second metric for lensing).
